facts.text: Prime Minister Pandit Nehru adopted the middle path rather than any extremes, and India gave preference to a model of 'mixed economy'.
facts.quote: Our Prime Minister Pandit Nehru adopted the middle path rather than taking recourse to any extremes. ... we gave preference to a model of 'mixed economy'.

facts.text: In a capitalist system the means of production are privately owned; in a socialist economy they are owned by the State in the name of the society. A mixed economy works both in the private and the public sector.
facts.quote: In a capitalist system, the means of production are privately owned. In a socialist economy, the means of production are owned by the State in the name of the society. A mixed economy works both in the private and the public sector.

facts.text: Public Sector: industries completely under the control and management of the government, for example production of defence equipment.
facts.quote: (1) Public Sector : The industries in this sector are completely under the control and management of the government. For example, production of defence equipment.

facts.text: Private Sector: industries owned by private industrialists, supervised and controlled by the government too, for example consumer goods.
facts.quote: (2) Private Sector : The industries in this sector are owned by private industrialists. Of course, the government supervises and controls them too. For example, consumer goods.

facts.text: Joint Sector: some industries are owned by private industrialists, while some are run under government management.
facts.quote: (3) Joint Sector : In this sector, some industries are owned by private industrialists, while some are run under government management.

facts.text: Defence, scientific research, education, roads, railways, waterways, sea port and airport development need huge capital and give delayed returns; few private industrialists invest, so the government has to take the initiative.
facts.quote: The industries like defence, scientific research, education, roads, railways, waterways, sea port and airport development require huge capital investment but the returns in these areas are delayed. Not many private industrialists are keen to invest in these areas. In such a situation, the government has to take the initiative.

facts.text: The industrial policy of 1973 increased the speed of development; the government focused on small scale and cottage industries and paid more attention to the cooperative sector.
facts.quote: The industrial policy of 1973 increased the speed of development. ... The government focused on the development of small scale industries and cottage industries. Government also started paying more attention to the cooperative sector.

facts.text: India established the Planning Commission in 1950 with Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru as its Chairman.
facts.quote: India established the Planning Commission in 1950 with Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru as its Chairman.

facts.text: Fundamental principle of planning: proportionate distribution of the resources of a country and appropriate use of the human resources to fulfil the needs of the people.
facts.quote: A general principle of planning is the proportionate distribution of the resources of a country and the appropriate use of the human resources to fulfil the needs of the people.

facts.text: Goals of planning included increasing national income, rapid industrialisation focusing on basic industries, self-sufficiency in food grain, controlling population growth by family planning and making the economy self-sufficient.
facts.quote: (1) Increase in the national income. (2) Bring about rapid industrialisation by focusing on the basic industries. ... (7) Bring the growth in population under control by family planning. ... (10) Make the economy self-sufficient.

facts.text: First Five Year Plan (1951-1956): expenditure mainly on agriculture, social development, irrigation and flood control and more; it laid the foundations of planned economic development.
facts.quote: First Five Year Plan (1951-1956): The expenditure in this plan was primarily on agriculture, social development, irrigation and flood control ... This plan consisted of measures to lay the foundations of planned economic development.

facts.text: Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961) had ambitious goals of industrialisation; iron and steel industries were set up at Durgapur, Bhilai and Rourkela.
facts.quote: Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961): This plan had ambitious goals of industrialisation. Iron and steel industries at Durgapur, Bhilai and Rourkela

facts.text: In the Second Plan: chemical fertilisers plant at Sindri, rail engine factory at Chittaranjan, factory of railway bogies at Perambur, ship building factory at Vishakhapattanam.
facts.quote: Chemical fertilisers plant at Sindri; rail engine factory at Chittaranjan; factory of railway bogies at Perambur; Ship building factory at Vishakhapattanam and other heavy industries were set up in the Public Sector.

facts.text: Huge dams like Bhakra-Nangal and Damodar were built in the Second Plan to make water available for agriculture.
facts.quote: Huge dams like Bhakra- Nangal, Damodar, etc. were built to make water available for agriculture. It led to increase in the national income.

facts.text: Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) aimed at a balance in industries and agriculture.
facts.quote: Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) : This plan was aimed at bringing about a balance in industries and agriculture.

facts.text: After the third plan, three one year plans were implemented (1966 to 1969), a period of intense famine; due to the invasion by China and war with Pakistan the government had to focus on defence.
facts.quote: After the third five year plan, three one year plans were implemented (1966 to 1969). This was a period of intense famine. Due to the invasion by China and war with Pakistan, the government had to focus on defence rather than development related tasks.

facts.text: Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-1974): aimed at self-reliance and a socialistic pattern of society; 14 major banks were nationalised; the economy bore the burden of the Bangladesh War and its refugees.
facts.quote: Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-1974): ... pay attention to establishing a socialistic pattern of society. 14 major banks in the country were nationalised. This plan did not succeed as expected. The economy had to bear the burden of the Bangladesh War.

facts.text: Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1979) aimed at making India economically self-sufficient by alleviating poverty, including a public distribution system; the goals of removing poverty and increasing employment were not achieved.
facts.quote: Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1979) : This plan was designed with the goal of making India economically self-sufficient by alleviating poverty. ... During the fifth plan, it was not possible to achieve the goals of removal of poverty and increase in employment.

facts.text: In the 1977 general elections the Congress Party was defeated and the Janata Party came to power.
facts.quote: In the 1977 general elections, the Congress Party was defeated. The Janata Party came to power.

facts.text: The new government ended the fifth plan towards the end of March 1978 and started the Rolling Plan from April 1978, but it failed.
facts.quote: The new government ended the fifth plan towards the end of March 1978 and started the Rolling Plan from April 1978, but it failed.

facts.text: In 1980 the Congress party came to power in the Lok Sabha elections and closed the Rolling Plan.
facts.quote: In 1980, general elections were held for Lok Sabha. The Congress party came to power. The Congress government closed the system of the Rolling Plan and again started planning like before.

facts.text: Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-1985) stressed alleviation of poverty and employment generation, and a population policy so that people adopted the small family norm voluntarily.
facts.quote: Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-1985) : This plan also stressed upon alleviation of poverty and employment generation. ... shape and implement a population policy so that people adopted the small family norm voluntarily

facts.text: Programmes of the sixth plan: Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP), Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP), National Rural Employment Programme (NREP), Salem Steel Plant.
facts.quote: The following programmes were implemented in the sixth five year plan: Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP). Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP). National Rural Employment Programme (NREP). Salem Steel Plant.

facts.text: Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-1990) laid stress on food, employment and productivity, aiming at a yearly increase in national income of 5%.
facts.quote: Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-1990): This plan laid stress on food, employment and productivity. ... to achieve an yearly increase in national income of 5% and increase food grain production.

facts.text: The seventh plan started Jawahar Rojgar Yojana, India Awaas Yojana and the Scheme of 10 lakh wells; it proved important for employment generation.
facts.quote: Jawahar Rojgar Yojana * India Awaas Yojana * Scheme of 10 lakh wells. The Seventh plan proved to be important from the point of view of employment generation.

facts.text: Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-1997) gave a lot of scope to the private sector; it aimed to maintain growth in national income at 6.5% and remove illiteracy by expansion of primary education.
facts.quote: Eight Five Year Plan (1992-1997): This plan gave a lot of scope to the private sector. The plan had the following features: to maintain the rate of growth in national income at 6.5% ... to remove illiteracy by expansion of primary education.

facts.text: Programmes of the eighth plan: Pradhanmantri Rozgar Yojana, Mahila Samriddhi Yojana, Rashtriya Samajik Arthik Sahayya Yojana, Midday Meal Scheme, Indira Mahila Scheme, Ganga Kalyan Scheme.
facts.quote: Pradhanmantri Rozgar Yojana * Mahila Samriddhi Yojana * Rashtriya Samajik, Arthik Sahayya Yojana * Midday Meal Scheme * Indira Mahila Scheme * Ganga Kalyan Scheme

facts.text: During the eighth plan the private sector grew in importance; the plan reflected the liberalisation and free market policy adopted in 1991.
facts.quote: During the eighth plan, the importance of the private sector grew. This plan is a reflection of the liberalisation and free market policy adopted in 1991.

facts.text: Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002) focused on agriculture and rural development; communication and the service sector progressed as expected.
facts.quote: Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002) : This plan focused on agriculture and rural development. ... In this plan, the progress of communication system and service sector was achieved as per the expectations.

facts.text: Schemes started in the ninth plan included Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana, Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Pradhanmantri Gram Sadak Yojana.
facts.quote: The following schemes were started during this plan : Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana, ... Antyodaya Anna Yojana, Pradhanmantri Gram Sadak Yojana, etc.

facts.text: During the tenure of Pandit Nehru and Lal Bahadur Shastri, banking was a monopoly of the private sector.
facts.quote: During the tenure of Prime Ministers Pandit Nehru and Lal Bahadur Shastri, banking was a monopoly of the private sector.

facts.text: The government nationalised the 'Imperial Bank' in 1955 and it was converted into State Bank of India.
facts.quote: the government nationalised the 'Imperial Bank' in 1955 and it got converted into State Bank of India.

facts.text: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 banks on 19th July 1969, including Allahabad Bank, Bank of Baroda, Bank of Maharashtra and Punjab National Bank.
facts.quote: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 banks on 19th July 1969. These include : Allahabad Bank, Bank of Baroda, Bank of India, Bank of Maharashtra, ... Punjab National Bank

facts.text: In 1980, six more banks were nationalised.
facts.quote: In 1980, six more banks were nationalised.

facts.text: Banks were nationalised to cover deficits while implementing schemes, and so that their profits would come into the government treasury.
facts.quote: Nationalisation of banks was essential to cover the deficits if they occurred while implementing different schemes. Also the profits of these banks would come into the government treasury once they were nationalised.

facts.text: Lal Bahadur Shastri undertook the experiment of the Green Revolution to overcome food shortages and drought.
facts.quote: Lal Bahadur Shastri undertook the experiment of the Green Revolution in order to overcome food shortages and drought.

facts.text: The 'Congress Forum for Socialist Action' demanded nationalisation of commercial banks; even the Communist Party supported this demand.
facts.quote: 'Congress Forum for Socialist Action', a group in the Congress party inspired by socialist ideas made a demand for nationalisation of commercial banks. Even the Communist Party supported this demand.

facts.text: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi announced the 20-point programme on 1st July 1975 to make efforts towards rapidly becoming a developed nation.
facts.quote: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi announced the 20-point programme on 1st July 1975 and resolved to make efforts towards rapidly becoming a developed nation.

facts.text: 20-point programme provisions included land ceiling, minimum wages for workers, freeing bonded labour, prevention of tax evasion and smuggling, and improving the textile industry by developing the handloom sector.
facts.quote: (1) Land ceiling ... minimum wages for workers ... (2) ... freeing bonded labour. (3) Prevention of tax evasion, economic crimes and smuggling. ... (5) Improvement in the textile industry by developing handloom sector

facts.text: The first textile mill was started in Mumbai in 1854 by Kawasjee Dawar.
facts.quote: The first textile mill was started in Mumbai in 1854 by Kawasjee Dawar.

facts.text: Mills started in Dadar, Paral, Bhaykhala, Shivdi, Prabhadevi and Worli; this part came to be known as Girangaon or 'town of mills'.
facts.quote: Eventually, mills started in Dadar, Paral, Bhaykhala, Shivdi, Prabhadevi and Worli. This part came to be known as Girangaon or 'town of mills'.

facts.text: Mahatma Jotirao Phule's associate Narayan Meghaji Lokhande's efforts resulted in the weekly Sunday holiday for mill workers from 1st January 1882.
facts.quote: Mahatma Jotirao Phule's associate Narayan Meghaji Lokhande's efforts resulted in the weekly Sunday holiday for mill workers from 1st January 1882.

facts.text: In the Diwali of 1981 workers expected a 20% bonus; the Rashtriya Mill Mazdoor Sangh agreed upon 8 to 17% without taking the workers into confidence, causing unrest.
facts.quote: In the Diwali of 1981, the workers expected to get a bonus of 20%. The Rashtriya Mill Mazdoor Sangh ... agreed upon 8 to 17% bonus without taking the workers into confidence. The cut in the bonus proved to be the cause of unrest.

facts.text: Workers of 65 mills came together and Dr Datta Samant led the strike; on 18th January 1982 two and a half lakh workers went on strike and Girangaon mills stopped running.
facts.quote: Workers of 65 mills came together and Dr Datta Samant led the strike. On 18th January 1982, two and a half lakh workers went on a strike. Girangaon mills stopped running making it seem like Mumbai's heart stopped throbbing.

facts.text: Chief Minister Barrister A. R. Antulay set up a committee; later Chief Minister Babasaheb Bhosale insisted he would talk only with the Rashtriya Mill Mazdoor Sangha; Dr Datta Samant demanded that the law be revoked.
facts.quote: The Chief Minister of Maharashtra, Barrister A. R. Antulay set up a committee to solve this issue. Later Babasaheb Bhosale became the Chief Minister ... he would talk only with the Rashtriya Mill Mazdoor Sangha. Dr Datta Samant demanded that the law be revoked.

facts.text: The workers started a 'Jail Bharo Agitation'; in September 1982 one and a half lakh workers marched on the Legislative Assembly of Maharashtra.
facts.quote: The workers started a 'Jail Bharo Agitation'. In September 1982, one and a half lakh workers took a march on the Legislative Assembly of Maharashtra State. It didn't help at all.

facts.text: The strike completed a year - the first strike to have gone on for a year; about one and a half lakh workers became unemployed.
facts.quote: The strike completed a year. This was the first strike to have gone on for a year. In this period, about one and a half lakh workers became unemployed.

facts.text: As polyester came into greater demand, mills moved from Mumbai to Surat in Gujarat; the Central government nationalised 13 textile mills.
facts.quote: As polyester had come into greater demand than cotton cloth ... The mills moved from Mumbai to Surat in Gujarat. The Central government nationalised 13 textile mills.

facts.text: Anna Bhau Sathe, Shahir Amar Sheikh and Shahir Sable were popular for programmes aimed at public education; poets like Narayan Surve and Namdev Dhasal portrayed workers' real life in poems.
facts.quote: Anna Bhau Sathe, Shahir Amar Sheikh, Shahir Sable were popular for their programmes aimed at public education. Poets like Narayan Surve, Namdev Dhasal, etc. portrayed the real life of the workers through their poems.

facts.text: 1991: after the 10th General Elections P. V. Narasimha Rao became Prime Minister and, with Dr Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister, adopted the new economic policy linking India's economy with the global economy.
facts.quote: The year 1991 is very important in the history of modern India. After the 10th General Elections, P. V. Narasimha Rao became the Prime Minister of India. With Dr Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister, he adopted the new economic policy of linking India's economy with the global economy.

facts.text: Before the Rao government, Chandra Shekhar was Prime Minister and inflation was 17%; growth had gone down by 1.1% and foreign exchange reserves could last for imports only for a week.
facts.quote: Before the P. V. Narasimha Rao government took charge, Chandra Shekhar was the Prime Minister. During his tenure the rate of inflation was 17%. Economic growth rate had gone down by 1.1%. India had foreign exchange reserves only enough to last for imports for a week.

facts.text: In May 1991 the government tried to control the situation by selling some of its gold reserves and mortgaging some.
facts.quote: In May 1991, the government had tried to control the situation by selling some of its gold reserves and by mortgaging some.

facts.text: The V. P. Singh government had incurred a liability of over 10 thousand crore rupees by waiving off the loans of all farmers.
facts.quote: Before the Chandra Shekhar government, the V. P. Singh government had incurred a liability of over 10 thousand crore rupees on the economy by waiving off the loans of all farmers.

facts.text: Foreign loan rose from 2350 crore dollars in 1980-81 to 8380 crore dollars in 1990-91; foreign exchange reserves were only 100 crore dollars, with oil prices up due to the invasion of Kuwait by Iraq.
facts.quote: In 1980-81 foreign loan was 2350 crore dollars. It increased to 8380 crore dollars in 1990-91. At this time, India had foreign exchange reserves of only 100 crore dollars. This also had the background of the increased oil prices due to the invasion of Kuwait by Iraq.

facts.text: Dr Manmohan Singh removed restrictions on foreign investments, restricted the licence system to 18 industries and opened the public sector to investment by private industries.
facts.quote: He removed the restrictions on foreign investments. He restricted the licence system to 18 industries. ... he opened up the public sector for investment by private industries.

facts.text: To bring the share market under control, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was established in 1988; the National Stock Exchange was computerised.
facts.quote: In order to bring the share market under control, he established the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in 1988. National Stock Exchange was computerised.

facts.text: India recovered the gold mortgaged with the Bank of England; opening the telecom sector spread mobile phone services; Dr Manmohan Singh signed the WTO agreement and launched privatisation, liberalisation and globalisation.
facts.quote: India could recover the gold mortgaged with the Bank of England. ... As the government opened up the telecom sector, mobile phone services started all over the country. Dr Manmohan Singh signed the agreement with the World Trade Organisation and launched the policy of privatisation, liberalisation and globalisation.

facts.text: In 1995 India became a member of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), whose objectives include free trade between countries.
facts.quote: In 1995, India became a member of the World Trade Organisation (WTO). The organisation had the following objectives: to free trade between countries

facts.text: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) existed at the international level before the WTO and regulated commerce.
facts.quote: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) existed at the international level before the World Trade Organisation came into being. It regulated commerce.

facts.text: India signed SAPTA, removed import restrictions on several commodities for SAARC countries and opened up the insurance sector to private and foreign investment.
facts.quote: India signed the South Asian Preferential Trade Arrangement (SAPTA) ... India removed the import restrictions on several commodities for SAARC countries. ... India opened up the insurance sector to private and foreign investment.
